description: Integrating Climate Change into the U.S. National Estuarine Research Reserve System is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; National Estuarine Research Reserve System. The National Estuarine Research Reserve System (NERRS) protects more than 1.3 million acres in 29 reserves in 23 states and Puerto Rico. Coverage: the United States (2008). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: The National Estuarine Research Reserve System (NERRS) protects more than 1.3 million acres in 29 reserves in 23 states and Puerto Rico. NERRs across the country are working to integrate climate change into their activities by increasing monitoring of climate change at reserve sites, assessing impacts and vulnerabilities, and providing education and training to the public and policy makers.
